title: Enclose a rectangular footprint with walls of a named type and confirm the corners join
task: Create four Wall elements from Line segments on a Level with Wall.Create, choosing a WallType by name (falling back to any Basic wall type), so the footprint closes and every corner is joined. Verify wall-end joins with LocationCurve.get_ElementsAtJoin; WallUtils.IsWallJoinAllowedAtEnd is only the allow-join toggle and JoinGeometryUtils.AreElementsJoined measures geometry joins.

miss.surfaced: BuiltInParameter and PostableCommand noise; JoinGeometryUtils did not appear

pitfalls.symptom: JoinGeometryUtils.AreElementsJoined returns false for freshly created walls that visibly meet at their corners, so the task looks failed; WallUtils.IsWallJoinAllowedAtEnd returns true even for a wall with nothing at its end.
pitfalls.cause: AreElementsJoined reports geometry joins (the Join Geometry command's effect), which newly created walls do not have; IsWallJoinAllowedAtEnd reports the Allow/Disallow Join toggle, not whether a join exists.
pitfalls.fix: Read ((LocationCurve)wall.Location).get_ElementsAtJoin(0) and (1): a joined end lists at least one element (step 6). Use IsWallJoinAllowedAtEnd only as the precondition.

pitfalls.symptom: The wall type lookup finds nothing and the script throws or picks a curtain wall type.
pitfalls.cause: Type names are case-sensitive and differ between templates; every WallType (Basic, Curtain, Stacked) comes back from OfClass(typeof(WallType)).
pitfalls.fix: Filter on WallType.Kind == WallKind.Basic and fall back to the first Basic type when the wanted name is absent.

pitfalls.symptom: Location curves or joins read back wrong immediately after Wall.Create.
pitfalls.cause: Geometry is not resolved until the document regenerates.
pitfalls.fix: Call doc.Regenerate() inside the block before reading geometry or joins.
